external_entities.name: Customer
external_entities.description: A customer who browses and orders socks through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and place orders.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app, which stores customer information, hands orders to SIMS, and receives catalogue changes.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that dials the number stored against an order and faxes a customer confirmation.
processes.source_excerpt: the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: marketing spreadsheet
processes.description: The spreadsheet containing the catalogue and macros that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
processes.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: The customer browses and places orders through the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: talk to API
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API over HTTP.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.description: The web API keeps customer names, addresses, and payment-card information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and card information

data_flows.name: hand over order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order over to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
data_flows.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop hosting the spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a mobile app rather than a website or web application.

assumptions.assumption: The fax gateway presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the component as a fax gateway that sends faxes.

assumptions.assumption: The marketing spreadsheet presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes macros in a spreadsheet rather than a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The user database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains customer names, addresses, and payment-card information.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains delivery addresses, which are personal information.
